segmentation: stem as stated: ú-da-nu = ú- (2nd person) + -da- (infix) + nu (Schuster 1974 p. 146)
notes: Schuster p. 146 'Wortstamm nu „gehen“', also p. 97; Kammenhuber 1969 p. 527 gives the same verb as nuu̯a [nuu̯] „kommen, gehen“ (= Hitt. pai-, u̯a-). Same Hattic stem is the Kammenhuber form for slot 11, so the two slots are not independent (§3.5).
Schuster p. 96 'aleb „Zunge“' (main discussion in his part 2, not viewed); p. 102 u̯aₐ-ša-aḫ a-li-ib „die bösen Zungen“. Not in Kammenhuber 1969.
grammatical item: see data/morphology.md

Schuster's only forms glossed 'come' are (a) a-ša-a „komm herein!“ (pp. 31-32), his translation of a monolingual Hattic recitation, i.e. a gloss from context only (§1.2: doubtful), and (b) ut-ta-a „komm herbei!“ (p. 147, tentative); his bilingual forms with Hittite uizzi 'comes' (ta-aš-te-e-ta-nu-u-u̯a p. 138) are built on the stem nu, which he glosses „gehen“ (slot 3). Under A3 precedence Schuster's form fills the slot. Kammenhuber 1969 p. 527 glosses nuu̯a „kommen, gehen“ without doubt: if that form were taken instead, this slot would be secure (sensitivity, see README).

Kammenhuber p. 444 n. 1, 466, 518 („Korrekt sind: tumil „Regen““); variant tumin a scribal error. Schuster gives only u̯aₐ/u̯iᵢ-bi-zi-il = Hitt. 'rain and wind', glossed „Regenböe“ (p. 99), which is not the slot meaning, so Schuster gives no form for this slot.
grammatical item: see data/morphology.md

segmentation: stem as stated; e.g. *ni-i-bu-e = (n)i- (1st person) + bu + -e (present) „wir machen“ = Hitt. iyaweni (p. 93)
notes: Schuster p. 89 'bu „machen“', bilingual p. 93; a-am-bu = Hitt. iet (p. 110). Disagreement: Kammenhuber 1969 p. 528 gives pu(?) „machen“ as doubtful.

segmentation: ḫa-ai-u̯aₐ-ib = ḫa- + -ai- (1st person possessive) + vae + -b (Schuster p. 97); li-e-u̯aₐ-e-el „sein Haus“ (p. 92, 137)
notes: Schuster p. 97 'Wortstamm vae- „Haus“'. Kammenhuber 1969 p. 467 gives p/u̯eₑl [fel] „Haus“ (= Hitt. É/parn-).

Schuster p. 93: tiuz (duplicate ziuz) = Hitt. NA4peruna- „Felsen“ (rock; slot is stone/rock); full discussion in his part 2 (not viewed). His restored zi-i-u̯[š?] „Felsen/Stein“ (pp. 93-94) is marked doubtful by him. Kammenhuber 1969 p. 454/504 gives pip = Hitt. NA4 „Stein“.

segmentation: unsegmented (Schuster p. 126 mentions -ḫ only as a possible adjective suffix)
notes: Schuster p. 86: ti-it-ta-aḫ-zi-la-at = Hitt. šalli GIŠŠÚ.A „der grosse Thron“ (tittaḫ = šalli, after Laroche); p. 126 tittaḫ „gross“, „erhaben“. Kammenhuber's ḫun (from ḫun-zinar „Groß-Musik“) is doubtful.
grammatical item: see data/morphology.md
Kammenhuber p. 535 anna „dies(?)“; Laroche's „dies(er)“ (p. 535). Not in Schuster.

segmentation: unsegmented (only the stem form is attested)
gloss_as_given: „stehen, sich stellen” (= heth. arta(ri) „er steht, stellt sich”)
notes: Kammenhuber p. 526 antiu „stehen, sich stellen“ = Hitt. arta(ri); p. 509 'zeigt vermutlich antiu = heth. arta(ri)' (doubt marker 'vermutlich'); one poorly preserved bilingual. Not in Schuster.

Kammenhuber pp. 466, 478, 498, 518 („Korrekt sind: ... pipiz(z)il „Wind““; Hitt. ḫuu̯ant-). Schuster gives only u̯aₐ/u̯iᵢ-bi-zi-il „Regenböe“ (not the slot meaning) and cites pipiz(z)el „Wind“ only in a bibliography title, so he gives no form for this slot.

segmentation: li-e- (possessive) + bi- (plural) + in „Sohn“ + -u (Schuster p. 128, offered as his preferred but tentative analysis)
notes: Schuster p. 126: li-e-bi-nu = Hitt. DUMU.MEŠ „Söhne“ (Forrer, Laroche); gloss secure, but the stem in/en is his proposal (p. 128: singular unattested). Kammenhuber 1969 p. 447 gives pinu „Kind“ with doubt (pinu or inu?).

segmentation: a-aš-ši-i̯a = a-aš- + i̯a „sie gaben“ (p. 121); 'Als Verbalstamm bleibt i̯a übrig' (p. 122)
notes: Schuster pp. 92, 121-122 (bilingual = Hitt. pai-). Kammenhuber 1969 p. 526 ai̯a, (i)i̯a „geben“.
grammatical item: see data/morphology.md
Schuster p. 101 malḫib „gut“ (after Forrer); p. 143 = Hitt. aššu „Gutes“. Kammenhuber 1969 p. 466 malḫip. Both note the word is used as noun 'good (thing)' and adjective.

gloss_as_given: Wort für „Erde“; = dankuwai taknī „in die dunkle Erde“
notes: Schuster p. 107: word for „Erde“ (= Hitt. dankuwai taknī 'into the dark earth'); his 'wohl' concerns the stem shape, not the meaning. Kammenhuber 1969 p. 447 ištarrazil „Erde“. earth -> soil is a permitted shift.

Gloss 'hide' comes only from the Hittite rendering munnandu „sie mögen verbergen“; Schuster himself derives the root her/hir „bestimmen“ (p. 106). Kammenhuber 1969 p. 529 *ziḫer „sich verbergen (o.ä.)“, also doubtful.

gloss_as_given: „seine-Fell(e)” (= heth. KUŠNÍG.BÀRḪI.A „die Felle”; KUŠNÍG.BÀR „Fell, Teppich, Decke”)
notes: Glossed only through the Hittite equivalent KUŠNÍG.BÀR (translated „Fell“ after R. Werner); Kammenhuber's own word list (p. 447) gives šteraḫ as '(Nomen)' with no meaning. Not in Schuster.

Schuster gives two stems glossed „nehmen“ (= Hitt. dā-): miš (pp. 116, 120) and tuḫ (a-an-tu-uḫ, p. 116); both secure, attestation counts not stated, so the first in alphabetical order (miš) is taken (§1.1). Kammenhuber 1969 pp. 527, 529 has the same pair, miš(a) and tuḫ.

segmentation: i-tu-ú-e = i- (1st person) + tu + -e (present) „wir (werden) essen“ = Hitt. edueni (Schuster p. 93); u̯aₐ-aḫ-tu-u = Hitt. adanzi (p. 105)
notes: Disagreement: Kammenhuber 1969 p. 528 gives pu/u̯aₐu [f(a)u] „(fr)essen“ from a badly transmitted bilingual.
Schuster p. 103: = Hitt. GIŠ-ru „Holz“ (wood); 'Kein weiterer Beleg'. Kammenhuber 1969 p. 455 zeḫar/ziḫar.

segmentation: tu-uk-zi-ik = tu-k- + zik (Kammenhuber p. 530; she calls the prefix analysis unclear, p. 531)
gloss_as_given: „von oben auf etwas herab/hinab fallen” (= heth. -kan mauš- „fallen”)
notes: Kammenhuber p. 517, 530: tu-uk-zi-ik = Hitt. -kan maušta „er fiel“, one attestation (Moon myth, badly transmitted); 'bedeutet offenbar „von oben auf etwas herab/hinab fallen“'. Not in Schuster.

segmentation: u̯aₐ-ḫ-kun (segmentation from Kammenhuber 1969 p. 526; Schuster p. 105 leaves it open)
notes: Schuster p. 105: u̯aₐ-aḫ-ku-un = Hitt. aušta=at „sie sah es“ (Forrer 236). Kammenhuber 1969 p. 526 kun(nu) „sehen“ = Hitt. au(š)-. Schuster's a-an-ta-ab-nu „sie schauten an“ (p. 120) has a tentative stem.

segmentation: ippi-zinar = ippi + zinar „Musik“ (Kammenhuber p. 437, 452, after Laroche)
notes: Glossed only through the compound ippi-zinar „Klein-Musik“; the element is not glossed on its own. Not in Schuster.

Kammenhuber gives three bound locative prefixes rendered by Hitt. anda 'in(to)': ḫa-, pe-, ta-, all hedged ('Alle heth. Übersetzungen sind nur annähernde Wiedergaben'); all doubtful, so the first in alphabetical order is taken. A prefix, not a free adposition. Not in Schuster.
